The Philippines loses billions of dollars every year to floods and landslides, yet decisions about forests are still evaluated through the lens of short term economic returns.

More than 200,000 trees are slated for removal in Palawan for mining.

This is profoundly irresponsible.

Beyond the loss of trees, it increases the risk of watershed degradation, soil erosion, and flooding in one of the world's most climate-vulnerable nations.

Mining should not come at the expense of long-term environmental stability.
